Commentary.Commentary: The players are out in the middle. Kraigg Brathwaite and John Campbell will open the batting for West Indies. Yamin Ahmadzai will start the proceedings for Afghanistan.
How will Afghanistan be able to bounce back from this poor show with the bat? 19 overs left in the day. Can they take 2-3 wickets at least? Stay tuned for the Windies' reply.

Hard to explain Afghanistan's state of mind. What bit them? Do they be happy with 187 on a spinning surface? One reckons that it is 60 under par. Disappointing aspect is that they were not bounced out or beaten by pace. Pure off spin consumed them where only 4 batters showed some grit.

Bowled out under 70 overs. Now, it looks like a good toss to win. But at 84/1, Holder would have had his doubts. The wicket of Javed Ahmadi sparked a collapse, with Rahkeem Cornwall running through the Afghan batting line-up. The other bowlers were barely present, leave aside Holder, who chipped in with a couple of scalps.

We are back for the final session of the day. The West Indies players are out in the middle. Amir Hamza will be joined by Yamin Ahmadzai in the middle for Afghanistan. Jason Holder will start the proceedings for the final session.

It has all turned pear-shaped for the 'home' side. They were looking in good shape at 84/1 but then collapsed to 111/7. The 54-run stand between Zazai and Hamza did stave off some respect but they need to get at least 250 to be somewhat competitive. The pitch is turning and West Indies would like to bat only once. First, their aim would be to wrap up the Afghans well inside 200 and bat for a good chunk of the final session. Join us back at 2.30 pm local (0900 GMT).

Cornwall - the refresher! A wicket in the final over before Lunch and a wicket in the final over before Tea. He has taken 75 percent of the wickets to fall, putting Afghanistan right into a mire. What a session for West Indies - 5/75 in 30.2 overs - 4 of those going to the offie.

The ball hits his pads, Cornwall appeals and umpire Reiffel agrees. No DRS, no Hawk Eye available to assist us but to the naked eye, it seems like it might have been spinning down leg. TEA ON DAY 1!

With the pendulum slightly tilting towards the West Indies, it would be a challenge for the Afghan batsmen to play the likes of Chase, Cornwall and Warrican. The pitch being dry and the odd ball keeping low means that batting will be tough in the coming sessions. Do join us for the afternoon session shortly.

What was turning out to be a cold session turns out to be a good one for West Indies. After opting to bat things looked bleak as both Holder and Roach sprayed all around the pitch. The Afghan batsmen initially looked at sea but soon had their eyes set and the runs started to flow. To everyone's surprise Holder tossed the ball to the giant Rahkeem Cornwall. Cornwall started to generate uneven bounce and sharp turn as he scalped the wicket of Ibrahim Zadran, jolting the Afghanistan innings early on. As the Lunch break was nearing Jomel Warrican was introduced and he too was into the wickets column as he had the attacking Javed Ahmadi hole out to long off. Just when one thought that the session was at even stevens, Cornwall went onto get his second of the innings.

The umpires make the batsman wait as they are checking for a possible no ball but replays show that it was just behind the line. THAT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 1!

Floated delivery on middle, Ihsanullah defends it off the back foot.
Tossed up delivery on middle, Ihsanullah comes down the track and plays it back towards the bowler.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Flighted delivery on off, Javed defends it out.
BEATEN! Tossed up delivery outside off, Ahmadi looks to defend but misses it.
Floated delivery on off, Ahmadi keeps it out.

FOUR! Lucky for the batsman there. This time Cornwall gets the ball to kick up from the fuller length on this tossed up delivery. The ball spins in and Ahmadi going for the cut is cramped for the room. The ball takes the thigh pad and goes past the keeper and into the fence at fine leg. The umpire signals it as a leg bye.
Tossed up delivery on middle, Ahmadi flicks it to mid-wicket.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Flighted delivery on middle, Ihsanullah comes down the track and plays it back towards the bowler.
Floated delivery on middle, Ihsanullah blocks it off the back foot.
Tossed up delivery down the leg side, Ihsanullah looks to flick but misses it.

FOUR! Signs of uneven bounce. Warrican tosses one up on the leg stump, Ihsanullah looks to defend it to the leg side but the ball keeps low and takes the inner half of the bat and runs past the leg slip and into the fine leg fence.
Tossed up delivery on middle, Ahmadi defends it off the back foot.
Jomel Warrican is into the attack.
Floated delivery on middle, Ahmadi looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Floated delivery on off, Ahmadi looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads. The ball rolls towards first slip.
Flighted delivery on middle, Ahmadi defends it off the back foot.
Floated delivery on middle, Ahmadi defends it out.
Tossed up delivery on off, Ahmadi guides it towards third man. The batsmen pick up a couple.
Good length delivery on off, Ihsanullah keeps it out.
Full again on leg, Ahmadi flicks it towards fine leg. The batsmen cross ends.
FOUR! Good shot. Full delivery on middle, Ahmadi flicks it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Length delivery on off, Ahmadi taps it to point.
On a good length on off, Ahmadi defends it off the back foot.
Around off, nicely blocked out.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Around middle, Ihsanullah goes back and works it, just wide of short leg, towards mid-wicket.

Nice shot but good fielding as well. Full and around off, Ihsanullah gets down and sweeps it through square leg. Roston Chase gives it a good chase from deep mid-wicket and slides to stop the ball. They refer it upstairs to check whether his feet have touched the ropes but replays deem it fine. Two runs taken.
Around off again, solidly blocked out.
FOUR! Nicely played. Full and around off, Ihsanullah gets down and sweeps it through square leg!
Around off, solidly defended from the crease.

DRINKS BREAK. A no-hour, shall we say? A captain wins the toss, elects to field, perhaps looking at the moisture and juice on the wicket but his new-ball bowlers find no extract. Then a spinner comes on and strikes, albeit which is debatable. On the positive aspect, West Indies have done well to keep the run rate in check while Afghanistan have stuck to their basics, not playing any rash shot. If they bat well, they can make the Windies toil here.
BEATEN! Good length delivery outside off, Javed looks to defend but misses it.
On a good length on off, Ahmadi defends it off the back foot.
FOUR! Nice shot. Fuller length delivery on middle, Ahmadi flicks it through square leg for a boundary.

BEATEN! Beauty from Roach.  Ahmadi might have got his heart in his mouth. Kemar bowls one on a fuller length and makes the ball talk. Ahmadi who plays for the original line gets squared up as the ball swings away marginally. The ball whizzes past the outside edge and into the mitts of the keeper.
Outside off, Ahmadi leaves it alone.
On a good length on off, Ahmadi blocks it off the back foot.
Kemar Roach returns. 4-1-17-0 so far.
Floated delivery on off, Ihsanullah defends it out.
This is down the leg side again, now Ishanullah pads it away.
Full and down the leg side, Ihsanullah looks to flick but the ball goes off his pads towards leg slip.

Flighted delivery on leg, Ihsanullah looks to flick but misses it. It goes towards fine leg. The fielder from leg slip chases it and does well to stop it before the ropes. The batsmen get two runs. The umpire gives it as byes.
Ihsanullah walks in at number 3, replacing Ibrahim Zadran.

OUT! CAUGHT! A spinner takes the first wicket after a team elects to bowl first. Rahkeem Cornwall it is. Flighted delivery on middle, Zadran looks to sweep but the ball goes off something, taking the pad on its way, towards leg slip. Jason Holder over there dives to his left and takes it one-handed. They all appeal and immediately, umpire Paul Reiffel raises his finger! Hard to spot any inside edge there. No technology available either.
Flighted delivery on off, Zadran looks to defend but gets hit on the thigh pad.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
On a length on off, Ahmadi taps it to point.

LBW appeal! Wow. Anyone remembers the Tendulkar dismissal to McGrath, given by Bucknor in Australia? A similar case here. Holder bowls a short delivery on middle, Ahmadi looks to duck under it but gets hit on the shoulder. The ball lobs to the keeper but Holder appeals for LBW! Well, even if he ducked, surely that was not so low that it would be hitting the stumps?
Outside off, Javed offers no shot to this one.
Good length delivery outside off, Ahmadi leaves it alone.
Outside off, Ahmadi shoulders arms to this one.
Flighted delivery on off, Ibrahim defends it off the back foot.
Tossed up delivery on middle, Ibrahim flicks it to mid-wicket.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Floated delivery on middle, Ibrahim nudges it to square leg.
Flighted delivery on off, Ibrahim defends it out.

Oohhh.. turn! Full and flighted delivery on off, Ahmadi looks to defend but misses it. It hits his pads and goes over the stumps and past the keeper towards fine leg. The fielder chases it and does well to stop it before the ropes. John Campbell chases it down but slips while trying to throw the ball. The batsmen get three runs.
Full and outside off, Zadran strokes it through point and takes a couple.
Good length and on off, Zadran defends it to covers.
Length and around off, Zadran lets it be.
Outside off, Zadran defends it off the back foot towards covers.
Good length and on off, Zadran blocks it to the off side.
Outside off, left alone.
Spin and bounce! Cornwall tosses one up and on middle, Ahmadi prods forward and the ball takes his pads and lobs to the leg side.
Full and on off, Ahmadi defends it to the off side.
Full and on off, Ahmadi defends it off the front foot.
Tossed up on off, Ahmadi defends by coming right behind the line of the ball.
Full and on off, defended back to the bowler.
Flighted on off, Ahmadi defends it to short leg.
Rahkeem Cornwall to bowl his offies now.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover this time.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers where John Campbell dives to his left and makes a stunning stop.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Around off, pushed towards cover.
Around off, solidly blocked out.
Full and outside off, Ibrahim leans and drives it towards cover.

BRAVE LEAVE! First delivery that has done something and caused a thought in the mind of the batsman. Roach bowls one on a length and outside off, he brings the ball back into the batsman. Ahmadi leaves it for the keeper to collect it. The ball was really close to the off pole.
Good length and on off, Ahmadi defends it to the off side.
Length and around off, Javed blocks it to point.
Length and on off, Ahmadi blocks it to the off side.
Length and on off, Ahmadi defends it to point.
EDGY FOUR! Ahmadi looks to drive this length ball through the off side. The ball takes the outside edge and runs past point and into the fence for a boundary.
Fuller in length and on middle, Zadran defends it to mid on.
Length and on off, Zadran defends it off the back foot.
Full and on off, Zadran does well to get his bat down in time. He gets an inside edge onto his pads..
FOUR! Overpitched and it got the beating. Zadran comes on the front foot to this length ball and creams the drive through covers. The ball races to the fence in a flash.
Another length ball outside off and Zadran is happy to let that go.
Length and outside off, left alone.
Ahmadi cuts this length ball through point for a couple.
Ahmadi defends this length ball on off to the off side.
Fast bowlers do not like that. Roach was charging in but at the last moment, Ahmadi pulled out. Not ready, was he.
Zadran taps this length ball through point for a run.
Short and on middle, Zadran looks to pull it through mid-wicket but gets a bit of a top edge. The ball does not carry to long leg. A couple taken.
Outside off, defended of the back foot.

FOUR! CLASSY! There comes the first boundary of the game. Length and on off, Ahmadi takes a good stride forward and strokes it off the middle of the bat, through covers, for a boundary. Nice poise for the photographers, if any.
Good length and on off, Ibrahim pushes it through covers for a run.
Around off and on a length, Zadran blocks it off the outer half off his bat to point.
On a length and on off, Zadran blocks it to covers.
Length and on off, defended to mid on.
Length and around off, Zadran leaves it alone.
Full and on the pads, Ibrahim flicks it to square leg.
Fuller length around off and middle, Zadran looks to play it to the off side. The ball takes the inside edge and goes towards mid-wicket. A run taken.
Length and around off, Ibrahim defends it to point.
Fuller length on middle, Zadran defends it to mid on.
Outside off, blocked off the back foot by Zadran.
Good length and around off, Zadran strokes it through long off for a couple.
Full and angling into the pads, Ahmadi flicks it through mid-wicket for a run.
Outside off, Ibrahim is happy to leave it.
Outside off, left alone.
Good length and around off, Ahmadi taps it past point. The batsmen scamper for a run. Afghanistan are off the mark here.
Length and outside off, Javed leaves it for the keeper.
Good length and around off, Javed blocks it to point.
Length ball on off, Ahmadi defends it to the off side.
Jason Holder to share the new ball with Roach.
Back of a length outside off, well blocked out. A harmless maiden over, nothing happening with the new ball.
Around off, coming in with the angle, solidly blocked out.
Outside off, IZ lunges to defend but gets a thick outside edge. Falls short of third slip.
Around off, coming in, Ibrahim looks to flick but the ball comes in, takes the inside edge and goes to square leg. Seam movement was late.
Full and around middle, pushed towards mid on.
A length ball, around off, coming in with the angle, watchfully defended from the crease.

The anthems are done and the players are out in the middle. Ibrahim Zadran and Javed Ahmadi will open for the Afghans. KEMAR ROACH, one of two seamers in the side, will start off proceedings with the new ball. Zadran to face. Here we go...
We are all set for the day and game to begin. The national anthems are being played. West Indies' first.

WEST INDIES (PLAYING XI) - Kraigg Brathwaite, John Campbell, Shai Hope, Shamarh Brooks, Roston Chase, Shimron Hetmyer, Jason Holder (c), Shane Dowrich (wk), Rahkeem Cornwall, Kemar Roach and Jomel Warrican.

AFGHANISTAN (PLAYING XI) - Ibrahim Zadran, Javed Ahmadi, Rahmat Shah, Ihsanullah, Asghar Afghan, Amir Hamza (DEBUT), Afsar Zazai (wk), Rashid Khan (c), Nasir Jamal (DEBUT), Yamin Ahmadzai and Zahir Khan.
TOSS - Interesting. Jason Holder has won the toss and ELECTED TO FIELD! Who does that in India? Brave call. Let us see how their quicks make use of the pitch upfront.

WEATHER - It is a hazy morning, with winter setting in the northern parts of India. That also means early sunset, which could cause the issue of bad light around 4 in the evening. The humidity is a massive 83 percent, which means the players will sweat it out post Lunch.

A Test match in India, not involving India. How many times do you see that? Thanks to the BCCI, Afghanistan are allowed to play their 'home' fixtures in this country and that is the reason for them hosting Ireland earlier, then Bangladesh and now, West Indies. After being  drubbed 0-3 in the ODIs, the Afghans did really well to come back hard in the T20Is. How will the Test fare though? If it is going to spin, then their spinners come into the fray. But then, West Indies are by no means, mugs with the bat. A fascinating encounter awaits us. Hello and a warm welcome to the one-off Test between Afghanistan and West Indies in Lucknow.
